column1: 8|automatic|The revenant itself refuses to stay gone: it returns to hand after each strike. Lower damage pays for repeatability without searching a pile.
10|automatic|The exile abandons a random possession before drawing new prospects; playing valued cards first narrows the remaining payment pool.
16|automatic|The gravedigger buries the most recently laid-down body, a visible fresh grave rather than a menu of corpses.
17|automatic|Confession relinquishes a burden from the held pool; the player can first play what they intend to preserve.
23|choose-offering|A willing sacrifice depends on choosing the offering. This deliberate irreversible payment is the central ritual, not an incidental discard.
26|automatic|The raven takes the nearest freshly abandoned object from the top of the visible pile.
52|automatic|The empty reliquary lets the oldest stored remnant pass away; the deepest record is a visible fixed target.
55|automatic|The seed roots into old spent matter and plants it for later growth; both recipients are fixed, with no quantity menu.
56|automatic|The ash scatters its own spent substance into a final strike instead of demanding an unrelated held victim.
65|automatic|The open book reopens the most recently closed page: the visible top discarded card.
72|automatic|The ancient cathedral draws its oldest lost remnant back from the foundations.
74|automatic|The crypt brings back the deepest, oldest buried card, matching its descending vaults.
76|automatic|The vines reclaim the nearest ruined layer and place it in the next position of the coming library.
79|automatic|The bridge connects the nearest stranded card to the hand without asking which crossing to use.
86|automatic|The submerged shrine lifts a relic from the deepest visible discard layer.
89|automatic|Ascension raises the lowest card into reach; the target follows the vertical motion in the art.
90|automatic|The depicted traveler takes its own card downward, then reveals a new prospect. No other traveler is selected.
91|recall-specific-card|Memory recalls one particular past experience. Keep this deliberate retrieval exception; Banish limits repeated unrestricted tutoring.
92|automatic|Oblivion spends and erases its own physical opportunity rather than randomly destroying an unrelated held card.
100|automatic|The marionette turns one held performer and fixes that same performer in its new pose, without selecting or remembering an earlier card.
101|automatic|The weaver joins the two most recently dropped strands into one coming sequence; the existing pile order supplies the pattern.
102|automatic|The unraveler pulls apart the nearest spent strand and uses that material for the strike; lower damage reflects the safer payment zone.
104|automatic|The undertaker lays the newly departed top card to rest.
107|plan-route-order|Planning the exact coming route is the cartographer’s whole effect. Retain this single deliberate ordering exception.
110|automatic|The resurrector raises the most recently fallen card; a fresh visible body gives a natural fixed recipient.
112|automatic|The locust consumes the next harvest before it arrives. Scry and earlier draws let play order protect valuable prospects; damage is reduced from the former hand-payment version.
114|automatic|The vulture feeds on fresh carrion, represented by the latest visible spent card.
122|automatic|The wrecked ship supplies its own destructive final impact. Its paired Lighthouse is also lost for the fight; no unrelated cargo-card choice is needed.
126|choose-route|Choosing a route is the wilderness expedition’s central decision. Retain that one selection, but remove the separate ordering prompt.
128|automatic|The bone orchard grows from the oldest buried remains, a fixed deep-pile nourishment source.
129|automatic|The market trades a held good for fresh goods. Earlier plays narrow its automatic payment pool.
130|automatic|The night market demands a risky surrendered possession for a large offer. Playing other cards first controls the eligible pool without a menu.
132|automatic|The empty banquet hall clears the latest feast’s visible leftovers.
134|automatic|Exploring the deep cavern brings its lowest lost object back into reach; this replaces arbitrary route selection.
140|automatic|The sunken library retrieves its oldest submerged volume from the deepest discard layer.
143|automatic|The clockwork city advances one arrival, then synchronizes the held machinery into its other state; no arrangement minigame is needed.
145|automatic|The sewing needle stitches the most recently dropped strand into the next part of the sequence.
146|automatic|The scissors cut the visible spent piece and cut through protection. Lower damage pays for the predictable discard payment.
147|automatic|The compass points out the next direction and advances one step, rather than asking the player to choose a direction for it.
156|choose-loaded-results|Loaded dice deliberately let the player pick the favorable outcomes. Retain that selection, with automatic existing order for every moved group.
160|automatic|The torn letter destroys its own message. It has no reason to erase another held subject.
163|automatic|The metronome alternates the two next beats. A fixed two-card reversal expresses its paired rhythm without choosing a permutation.
165|automatic|The lens brings the next subject into focus and reach, without turning magnification into a selection menu.
167|automatic|The comb straightens the held array into its encounter-starting orientation. Light here names a face, not moral worth.
170|automatic|The rag doll reassembles several recently discarded scraps. It returns a fixed pair and spends its repair opportunity.
172|automatic|The unequal two-in/one-out exchange keeps the asymmetric shape. The random loss happens after the new cards arrive.
173|automatic|Unity brings a newcomer into the held group, then keeps that whole group together.
174|automatic|The subject itself breaks into two striking fragments. Lower per-hit damage replaces the unrelated chosen sacrifice.
175|automatic|The two nearest past routes converge into one upcoming stream; the existing order avoids a second arrangement choice.
176|automatic|The departing figure takes its own lower route while a new prospect arrives from above.
179|automatic|The reaching hands pull new possibilities into the hand directly, instead of searching a past-card menu.
180|automatic|Repulsion pushes the entire held group away and admits a fresh set, preserving a clear physical cause and effect.
182|automatic|Levitation lifts the nearest discarded object back into the held space.
184|automatic|Frenzy loses a held resource unpredictably in its burst. Prior plays can protect important cards by narrowing that pool.
193|automatic|The tide carries the two nearest stranded objects back; hand space determines how many can fit, not a quantity prompt.
194|automatic|The ebb carries the nearest layer away and reveals what lay beneath. An earlier Scry or draw makes the fixed shift a play-order decision.
198|automatic|The smuggler slips its own card out of sight while bringing new goods into reach.
200|automatic|The depicted flag supplies its own fuel and is spent, rather than burning an unrelated held subject.
208|automatic|The ferryman brings an old departed card back across from the deepest side of the discard pile.
209|automatic|The auction exchanges an automatically surrendered held good for new offers; the player controls the remaining pool through prior plays.
210|automatic|The scavenger takes the nearest abandoned object, the visible top discard.
214|automatic|The stray hound retrieves the freshest abandoned trace rather than opening a recovery menu.
215|automatic|The archivist retrieves the oldest record and checks the resulting next entry; no catalogue search selection is required.
216|automatic|The bookworm consumes the oldest, most settled paper record in the pile.
217|automatic|The surveyor measures the next step and advances one, leaving route arrangement to the dedicated cartographer exception.
219|automatic|The sweep clears burning residue and the freshest spent soot; each recipient is explicit.
229|automatic|The dandelion disperses all its held seeds into future growth, replacing the quantity and individual seed choices.
234|automatic|The old skin itself is shed as the new possibility arrives; no other held object must be chosen.
236|automatic|The corpse flower feeds on the deepest buried matter to produce its Decay strike.
244|automatic|The silverfish eats the oldest stored paper rather than selecting a fresh page.
247|automatic|The quill brings the last written entry back as the next line.
248|automatic|The eraser removes the currently visible last entry from the spent pile.
251|filter-one-card|Selecting what passes through the sieve is its entire filtering action. Keep that one choice; avoid inventing an arbitrary light/dark filter or an extra discard-order choice.
252|automatic|The funnel narrows the whole held stream into one immediate card, with the rest queued in their existing order.
258|automatic|The water clock supplies a fresh measured flow and remains for another use. A full hand can prevent its self-return, making earlier plays matter.
259|automatic|The ladder lifts the nearest stranded card back into reach.
270|automatic|The funeral veil covers the most recently departed card.
272|automatic|The latest performer waits just behind the curtain, ready to return.
273|automatic|The long staircase raises the lowest visible lost card into the hand.
274|automatic|The well’s depicted traveler takes its own card downward, while another is drawn upward.
276|automatic|The sewer drains the lowest, oldest settled waste from the discard pile.
281|automatic|The counting house deposits a held asset for later rather than destroying it. Prior plays determine the remaining deposit pool.
285|automatic|The causeway exchanges a carried object with the nearest object across the divide. The incoming object is visible; earlier plays narrow the outgoing pool.
292|automatic|The abandoned fairground recalls its oldest past performance, rather than selecting among all memories.
295|automatic|The paved road supplies a fixed clear next step; it need not ask the traveler to design another route.
299|automatic|The jeweler restores the visible used ornament to its encounter-starting form before returning it.
305|automatic|The clockmaker restarts the latest spent moment as the next tick and observes the resulting sequence.
309|automatic|The scribe copies the oldest surviving record into the next blank position of the library.
310|automatic|The drinker consumes the freshest visible inked remnant as nourishment.
312|automatic|The portrait eraser removes the currently visible spent image.
316|automatic|The scent thief removes the freshest lingering trace, the last discarded card.
327|automatic|The spinner picks up the nearest dropped thread and feeds it into the next strand.
328|automatic|The shears sever the nearest spent strand instead of selecting an unrelated held subject.
330|automatic|The swallower consumes the most recently told story from the visible pile.
334|automatic|The eraser removes the next available path before it is taken. Scry and prior draws let the player plan around that erasure.
338|automatic|The oath breaker spends its own broken commitment, opening a new possibility without choosing another victim.
341|automatic|The mender restores the nearest discarded subject to its encounter-starting form; that is physical renewal, not a moral label.
342|automatic|The thief takes the nearest abandoned doll as it stands; unlike the mender, it does not restore its face.
343|automatic|The conductor reverses the next three entries as one fixed musical gesture, then reveals the next cue.
344|automatic|The improviser takes new material and loses one spontaneous element; its uncertainty is resolved automatically.
346|automatic|The wanderer crosses to the far, oldest tidal side. The incoming card is fixed; play order narrows the carried outgoing pool.
383|automatic|The renewing birch returns the oldest fallen material to future growth in the soil.
386|automatic|The fallen leaf itself passes out of use, rather than removing an unrelated memory.
403|automatic|The offered gloved hand delicately lifts the nearest lost object back into reach.
406|automatic|The basket’s own woven form comes apart into reeds; it does not arbitrarily destroy another card.
414|automatic|The loose thread pulls its own held form apart and leaves the fight.
422|automatic|The empty locket lets its oldest stored memory go.
424|automatic|The unusable melted key is itself cleared away; no unrelated second remnant is required.
429|automatic|The writing feather places the last recorded line back at the next position.
430|automatic|The blot obliterates the most recently exposed written entry.
432|automatic|The scraper removes the visible top layer of the spent portrait.
438|automatic|The empty needlecase itself has nothing left to offer and can be set aside.
457|automatic|The shaped hedge sends the next three steps back through a fixed winding route; Scry shows the new opening.
460|automatic|The dry fountain is exhausted and leaves the fight instead of inexplicably granting foresight or removing another object.
461|automatic|The golden atrium admits a newcomer and floods the whole held scene with light. The visit is spent rather than choosing an opening.
466|automatic|The mill consumes one automatically selected held input before producing two outputs; earlier plays narrow its feedstock.
471|automatic|The grand library retrieves its oldest stored volume; Memory retains the exceptional precise search role.
472|automatic|The forgotten archive loses its oldest stored record, mirroring the library’s fixed oldest-record retrieval.
476|automatic|The ship graveyard raises an old buried wreck from its deepest layer.
477|automatic|The ivory bridge simply carries the nearest stranded object back across, rather than creating an arbitrary exchange menu.
480|automatic|The deep stone stair raises the lowest stranded card back into reach.
486|automatic|The timeless tower reaches back to the oldest available moment and returns it.
